To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the perceived self-efficacy of students, teachers, and school faculties are important contributors to the cognitive development and functioning of the students in the schools.
perceived self efficacy is a major determinant of academic motivation and achievement.

The relationship between perceived self efficacy and academic achievement is mediated by motivation and cognitive strategies and that the effects of self efficacy are moderated by task characteristics and contextual factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role that students' and teachers' beliefs in their capabilities to organize and execute courses of action influence their cognitive, affective, motivational, and selection processes, which in turn influence their level of academic development.
how people perceive their own abilities to produce given levels of performance that affect outcomes in learning and other cognitively based tasks.
the ways in which perceived control beliefs influence cognitive development and cognitive functioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self efficacy is a major factor that affects the development of cognitive functioning and the level of functioning in academic areas.
perceived self efficacy plays a significant role in the cognitive development and functioning of students, teachers, and faculty members.
self efficacy is a key determinant of academic development and functioning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perceived efficacy of students, teachers, and school faculties are all related to academic achievement and development.
perceived self efficacy is a key determinant of cognitive development and functioning.
self efficacy beliefs are an important contributor to cognitive development and achievement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most important factor in determining the success of a school is the collective belief in their efficacy of the faculty.
the more we believe we are able to achieve our goals, the more likely we will be able to achieve them.
perceived self efficacy is a major factor in academic development and that it is important to understand the diverse ways in it contributes to cognitive development, learning, and achievement.
